headline: Every pack of ham checked, not a sample.
label: #FFF8EC
heroLede: Bertocchi has made smallgoods since 1972 and runs several brands of its own from Thomastown, including San Marino, Wurstel and Happy Pig. With that many products and brands going through packing, checking every seal, label and code by eye takes a lot of your team’s time. This is what a camera check could look like on a sliced smallgoods line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every vacuum pack is sealed flat across the end, with no creases and no film sitting loose. A leaker shortens shelf life and turns into a complaint once it is on the shelf.
labelLede: Leg ham and smoked ham look much the same through the film, and the brand on the pack can change from one run to the next. The camera checks every pack carries the right label for the run, straight and intact.
codeLede: Sliced smallgoods carry a use-by date, and in the Christmas ham rush there is little time to check codes by hand. The system reads the printed date and batch code on every pack and compares them with the product and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Casings, clips, glove pieces and packaging offcuts are all close at hand in a smallgoods plant. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four creased seals in fifteen minutes on Line 1. Check the vacuum sealer.
